requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected for four players
How the selected Pods are distributed and oriented
Tokens placed in the Intruder bag at setup
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for a four-player game. 2. Put the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next in Section B, then alternate Sections A and B; all start with the Locked side face up. 3. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults for four players).
answers.evidence: [1] Setup step 7: "Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players." [2] Setup step 7: "Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up." [3] Setup step 10: "Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player." Inference: for four players, add four Adults to the listed three Adults, for 7 Adults total.

requested_parts: How Objectives are filtered and dealt
When each player chooses one and what happens to the rejected card
Whether Eggs trigger the choice
answers.answer: 1. Remove from both the Corporate and Personal Objective decks every card requiring more players than are in this game; shuffle the decks separately and deal each player one of each, kept hidden. 2. At the first Encounter, each player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from the game without anyone looking at it. 3. Eggs do not trigger this choice; they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: [1] Setup step 16: "Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden." [2–3] First Encounter rule: "the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this."

requested_parts: Which cards are discarded to play a cost-2 Action card
Whether Contamination cards can pay the cost
How to resolve a card offering OR effects
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card itself plus two other Action cards, for 3 Action cards total. 2. Contamination cards cannot substitute for any payment. 3. Choose one of the OR effects; the printed payment remains the same for the chosen card.
answers.evidence: [1] Action Cost: "For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total." The printed-payment example states: "Captain's Basic Repairs has an extra cost of 2. Discard Basic Repairs itself + 2 other Action cards = 3 Action cards total." [2] Action Cost: "Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost." [3] Action cards: "To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one."

requested_parts: When Fire damage occurs after a Character acts then passes in a burning Room
Whether the Character can act again that Player Phase
Whether the Character may discard cards when passing
Whether later players' rounds cause further Fire damage to that Character
answers.answer: 1. Fire damage is one Light Wound at the end of that Character's own passing round, after declaring Pass. 2. No further normal Actions are allowed after passing for the rest of that Player Phase, though Interruption remains permitted subject to its requirements. 3. At the moment of passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Later players' rounds do not cause them another Fire wound that turn.
answers.evidence: [1,4] Turn Structure: "A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn)." Passing table: "Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn." [2] Passing table: "Normal Actions | You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below." [3] Passing table: "Hand cards | At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand."

requested_parts: What happens on entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter and Exploration effect
When and how the Noise roll is made and where its token goes
How Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination affect the Noise roll
answers.answer: 1. Flip the unexplored tile face up; reveal and resolve its Exploration token, set the Item Counter to the number shown (except the Nest and Room Covered With Slime have no Item count), then remove the Exploration token from the game. 2. After the Exploration result, because the Room is empty, make the ordinary Noise roll unless the Exploration result itself was Silence or Danger. On a 1–4 place Noise in the connected Corridor bearing that number; if that Corridor already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead. Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the destination; if none are eligible, place Noise in each connected Corridor without a marker. 3. Silence means no Movement Noise roll and nothing happens, unless the Character has Slime, in which case resolve Danger instead. Danger also replaces the roll. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not roll Movement Noise.
answers.evidence: [1] After entering a Room: "(1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule." Exploration Item Counter rule: "the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot." [2] After entering a Room: "A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders)." Noise roll: "Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead." [3] Exploration tokens: "Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead." Noise roll: "Danger: if there is an Intruder in a neighboring Room (and it is not in Combat with any Character), move it into this Room — all eligible Intruders move. If there are no Intruders in neighboring Rooms (or they are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one (counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance)." After entering a Room: "If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise."

requested_parts: Careful Movement's cost and what it replaces
When Careful Movement is forbidden
Whether it can cross a Closed Door
Whether a miniature may stop in a Corridor
answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the Noise roll after moving with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room entered. 2. It cannot be used while in Combat, and cannot be used if every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. 3. No: normal Movement restrictions apply, and a Closed Door blocks passage. 4. No one may stop in a Corridor; Characters and Intruders occupy Rooms (Escape Pod tokens are the exception for Characters).
answers.evidence: [1–2] Basic Actions: "Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat." [3–4] Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: "Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor." Also: "A Closed Door blocks the "neighboring" status for players' Movement."

requested_parts: Encounter sequence when a Noise roll selects a Corridor already holding Noise and Technical Corridors Entrance is connected
What happens to existing Noise
Where the drawn token goes, including Blank handling
How Surprise Attack is determined and who is targeted
Whether Contamination cards count in the comparison
answers.answer: 1. A duplicate Noise placement triggers an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space when connected; then draw one Intruder token, place its matching miniature if it is not Blank, and compare the token number to the triggering player's hand. 2. All connected Noise is discarded as the Encounter starts. If a Blank is drawn, instead place Noise in each connected Corridor and return the Blank to the bag; if it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if available. 3. Keep a non-Blank drawn token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned (it may return if that Intruder later hides in Technical Corridors). Return a Blank to the bag. 4. If the triggering player's hand has fewer cards than the number on the token, that player suffers a Surprise Attack; equal or more means nothing happens. The Intruder Attack target in a Surprise Attack is the Character who triggered the Encounter. 5. Yes. Action and Contamination cards both count in the hand comparison.
answers.evidence: [1,2,4,5] Encounter: "Resolve: 1. Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance). 2. Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below. 3. Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. 4. Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens." [2–3] Blank token rule: "place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears)." Non-Blank tokens may return if an Intruder of that type later hides by entering Technical Corridors. [4] Intruder Attack: "A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter". [Noise trigger] Noise roll: "A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead."

requested_parts: How Danger resolves when several neighboring Intruders are eligible
What happens when no neighboring Intruder is eligible
Whether an Intruder moving into the Character's Room is an Encounter
How Slime affects Silence
answers.answer: 1. All eligible Intruders in neighboring Rooms move into the Room; eligible means not in Combat with any Character. 2. If there are none eligible (there are no neighboring Intruders or all are in Combat), place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. 3. No. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; the Character and Intruder are in Combat. 4. With Slime, Silence resolves as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Noise roll: "Danger: if there is an Intruder in a neighboring Room (and it is not in Combat with any Character), move it into this Room — all eligible Intruders move. If there are no Intruders in neighboring Rooms (or they are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one (counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance)." [3] Encounters: "An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat)." [4] Noise roll: "Silence: nothing happens; no marker. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead."

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank token when Blank is drawn during an Encounter
Whether an Adult is added in this Encounter case and under what condition
What happens to Blank when drawn during bag development
answers.answer: 1. During an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in each Corridor connected to the Room; no Intruder miniature appears. The Blank returns to the bag. 2. Add an Adult token only if the Blank was the last token in the bag, and only if an Adult token is available. 3. During bag development, a Blank adds one Adult token to the bag if one is available (otherwise nothing happens), then the Blank returns to the bag.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Blank token in an Encounter: "place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears)." [3] Bag development: "Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag."

requested_parts: Where two Intruders attempting to move together through one Closed Door end
What happens to the Door and whether it can later close
Whether a Noise-triggered appearance is blocked by the Closed Door
answers.answer: 1. Both stay in the Room they attempted to leave; when several Intruders move from the same Room, they destroy the Closed Door simultaneously and all stay put. 2. The Door becomes Destroyed (laying token); ordinary effects cannot close a Destroyed Door again, and only the Plasma Torch Item can close it. 3. A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Corridor with a Closed Door is not blocked; it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: [1] Door tokens: "An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put)." [2] Door tokens: "Destroyed = lying token; movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it." [3] Door tokens: "If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door."

requested_parts: What happens to an injured Intruder miniature when it moves into Technical Corridors
What happens to its Injury markers, token and existing Noise there
Whether Characters or Door tokens may normally use/place into those Corridors
answers.answer: 1. It disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed from the board. 2. Discard all its Injury markers and return its Intruder token to the bag; the Noise marker already on the Technical Corridors space remains. 3. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card or the Technical Corridor Plans Item card. Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Technical Corridors: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.” [3] Technical Corridors: “Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic’s “Technical Corridors” Action card and the “Technical Corridor Plans” Item card).” “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Action-card cost and Ammo cost for ordinary Shoot versus Melee
Where each attack may target
Contamination handling for Melee
What happens on a miss for each
What a two-hit die result does
answers.answer: 1. Both are Basic Actions costing 1 Action card. Shoot also requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo and discards 1 Ammo; Melee has no Ammo payment. 2. Both target one Intruder in your Room. 3. Melee draws 1 Contamination card and puts it on top of your Action discard pile; Shoot has no Contamination draw. 4. A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries and no Wound to the shooter; a Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and inflicts 1 Serious Wound on the attacker. 5. A double-hit result causes 2 Injuries in Shoot, but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: [1] Basic Actions: “Shoot (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo) — attack an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in your Hand, discarding 1 Ammo from that Weapon’s card.” Action-cost rule: “Basic, Room and Item Actions have no played Action card to add to their printed cost; pay any separate Ammo, Item-component or other requirements as instructed.” Melee is listed among Basic Actions costing 1 Action card. [2] Shoot procedure: “Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room”; Melee: “choose 1 target Intruder in your Room.” [3] “Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die.” [4] “A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.” [5] Die results: “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers | 1 Injury to any Intruder type”.

requested_parts: How Larva death is checked after damage
How Adult death is checked
How Queen death is checked and when a Carcass is placed
What a Retreat arrow on a Queen check does
answers.answer: 1. A Larva dies at 1 Injury; no Carcass is placed. 2. For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and use only its blood value; blood less than or equal to current Injuries kills it, and its death places a Carcass in the Room. 3. For a Queen, draw 2 Intruder Attack cards and sum their blood values; if the sum is less than or equal to current Injuries, it dies and a Carcass is placed in the Room. 4. If either Queen card has a Retreat arrow, retreat is resolved instead of a numerical death result: draw an Event card, move the Queen through the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, and discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Intruder Injuries and death: “after any Injuries, put that many Injury markers on the Intruder’s base and check its Injury Effect. Compare current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.” The table states: “Larva | 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass”; “Adult | Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; “Queen | Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.” [4] Retreat rule: “during an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card’s blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card’s Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: When and in what order the two Intruders attack during Escape
Who is targeted
What happens if the Character dies
What happens if the Character survives into the empty unexplored destination
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each Intruder in the current Room, starting with larger types: Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva. 2. Escape attacks target the escaper. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. 4. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring unexplored Room; explore it normally, and since it is empty, make the Noise roll as usual after exploration unless an Exploration result replaces it.
answers.evidence: [1] Character Escape: “to leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5).” [2] Intruder Attack: “A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.” [3] Character Escape: “If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” [4] Character Escape: “If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored).” After entering a Room: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders).”

requested_parts: How the target is selected among several Characters and how ties are broken
How a non-Larva Intruder Attack hits or misses
What happens in a Larva attack instead
Where the Larva attack’s Contamination card is placed
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the Character with the First Player token or the next player in turn order. 2. For a non-Larva, draw an Intruder Attack card; a matching Intruder-type symbol means resolve the card’s effect, otherwise the attack misses. 3. A Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature from the board and place it on the target’s Character board. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing Larva remains, and the attack does not automatically kill the target. 4. The target gains 1 Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Intruder Attack: “with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order).” “For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder’s type, resolve the card’s effect; otherwise the attack misses.” [3] “Larva exception: draw no Attack card; use Infest below.” Infest: “A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target’s Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).” [4] Contamination: “When a Character ‘gets a Contamination card,’ draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether dressing one of three Serious Wounds prevents death from a further Light Wound
What a third Light Wound does
What Heal removes
Where a dead Character’s Corpse and Heavy Objects go
answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing ignores that Wound’s effect but the card still counts toward the three-wound limit, and a Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies upon any further Wound. 2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card as specified by the healing effect. 4. On death, put a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: [1] “A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious).” Dressing: “flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds.” [2] Light Wounds: “on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” [3] Heal: “remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.” [4] Death: “Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.”

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Canteen/Shower scan and which scan results are removed
How an Infected card is handled if no Larva is already on the Character board
How an Infected card is handled if a Larva is already present
Which cards Surgery scans/removes and how it handles Larva
Surgery cost and turn/hand consequences
answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan all Contamination cards in the Character’s hand only; remove all non-Infected scanned cards from the game. 2. An Infected result keeps the Infected card and places a Larva on the Character board if there was no Larva there before the scan. 3. If a Larva was already there, the Infected card stays and the Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room. 4. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand and discard, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva from the Character board if present. 5. Surgery costs 2 Action cards as a Room Action; afterward suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into the Action deck. The hand remains empty until the next turn.
answers.evidence: [1] Canteen/Shower table: “Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result.” The Room Actions state Canteen: “Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones”; Shower: “discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones.” [2–3] Canteen/Shower table: “Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board”; “Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.” [4–5] Surgery Room Action: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” Common Room Action requirements: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.”

requested_parts: How Shoot and Melee destroy uncarried Eggs
How Grenades and Molotov Cocktails affect uncarried Eggs
Which Melee penalties are waived on a miss versus retained on a hit
When and where Noise is rolled after attempts
When the Nest is considered destroyed
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. 2. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. A Molotov immediately destroys 1 Egg, and its Fire marker may continue destroying Eggs during later Fire Damage steps. 3. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound; a successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card to the Action discard pile. 4. Roll Noise after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll Noise in your own Room, not the Nest. 5. The Nest is destroyed when no Intruder Eggs remain in it; an Egg must be removed from the Nest’s Egg pool to meet this condition.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Egg destruction table: “Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below.” “Grenade | Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there.” “Molotov Cocktail | Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps.” [3] “Egg Melee penalties: a successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified.” [4] “Noise after an attack attempt: after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).” [5] Objective type: “Destroy the Nest — no Intruder Eggs may remain in it.” Inference: the Nest is destroyed when its Egg count is reduced to zero.

requested_parts: Conditions permitting entry into an Escape Pod and conditions preventing entry
What must happen during the entry attempt before boarding succeeds
Character and Heavy Object capacity
Choices and consequences at the start of later Player Phases while waiting
answers.answer: 1. Entry requires an Unlocked Pod with a free Character space in the corresponding Evacuation Section; no entry is permitted while that Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. Pay 2 Action cards for the Section Room Action. 2. Roll Noise; if an Intruder appears or is present in the Section, entry fails. 3. A Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 4. After boarding, you pass the current turn and remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass, launch, or exit free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Escape Pod Board: “pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail.” [3] Capacity: “2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space.” [4] Wait after boarding: “you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1).” Later rounds: “At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase | Choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2).”

requested_parts: Order of endgame checks
Outcome of two Damaged Engines
Outcome of a non-Earth destination and the Quarantine/Mars exception
Contamination check when a survivor has an Infected card or Larva
Whether launched Pod passengers undergo Contamination checks
answers.answer: 1. If at least one Character survived by hibernating or launching, resolve Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. 2. Two Damaged Engines make the ship explode; everything aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders, while launched Pod passengers are already away. 3. If the ship survives, a non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters; a sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars. 4. A survivor with any Infected Contamination card, or a Larva already on their board, shuffles all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard into a single deck and draws four; any Contamination card among the four kills them, whether Infected or not.
